verdicts.note: (not flagged verify) Romance in B-flat major, Op. 10 (Hudec 257), violin & piano, composed 1879, publ. Urbanek, Prague 1880; modern Supraphon edition EO 738 (1951). Wikipedia work list agrees (H 257, Op. 10, 1879). Recorded by Josef Suk / Josef Hala (Supraphon SU 3473-2).

(not flagged verify) Sonatina in D minor, Op. 27 (Hudec 114), 'instructive' sonatina, 3 movements, c. 11 min, composed 1869, publ. Urbanek 1887 (U. 369); violin part entirely in 1st-3rd positions (IMSLP); current Editio Barenreiter Praha H 1442 (fingering V. Snitil). Level 2 is reasonable.

The work exists (Hudec 199, Sonata in D major for violin and piano, 1875 per Wikipedia / 1876 per some CD booklets; recorded by Josef Suk and Josef Hala, Supraphon SU 3473-2, 2000) but I found NO published edition: it is not on IMSLP and no Barenreiter/Supraphon/Panton/CHF score turned up, so treat as unpublished/manuscript. (Also a lost/unpublished Sonata in C major, H 193, 1874.) If the owner decides to admit recorded-but-unpublished works, the title would be 'Sonata in D major' with no opus number.

gaps.title: Idyll (Selanka), Op. 16
gaps.scoring: clarinet or violin with piano (also with orchestra, orchestrated by Kovarovic); 1879
gaps.edition: Fr. A. Urbanek, Prague (early print, score + clarinet and violin parts); current Editio Barenreiter Praha H 3754 (EAN 9790006572342) 'Idyll, Op. 16 for clarinet (violin) and piano'
gaps.note: OPTIONAL / LOW PRIORITY: clarinet-primary piece with violin as the printed alternative; I found no violin recording. Second source: Wikipedia's Fibich work list (Op. 16, 1879, 'clarinet (or violin) and piano (or orchestra)'). The other violin works in Fibich's list (Clear Night H 183, Concert Polonaise H 238, Song without Words for 2 violins H 265, sonatas H 193/199) are recorded (Supraphon SU 3473-2) but I found no published editions, so they are NOT proposed. Gap check is complete for IMSLP (43 pages scanned) and Wikipedia.

existing_issues.issue: Catalogue number is doubtful. IMSLP and Wikipedia's work list give the Kubelik violin & piano arrangement as 'Poeme in D-flat major, Op. 39a' (taken from the Lento of the orchestral idyll At Twilight / V podvecer, Op. 39; the same music is No. 139 of the piano cycle Moods, Impressions and Reminiscences, Op. 41; Urbanek, Prague 1909, U. 1551). A Schott/Boosey listing uses 'Poeme op. 41/6'. Prefer IMSLP/Wikipedia. (Schindler's 'Souvenir poetique', G. Schirmer 1911, and Weninger's 1931 version are other arrangements of the same piece - not to be added.)
existing_issues.suggested_title: Poème in D-flat major, Op. 39a (arr. Kubelík)
